did: The planner proposed a split into six stories with 29 criteria.
It raised three questions for the owner.
decided: Re-plans keeping the owner's commits, and the owner's work getting checks, are left as true.
open: Whether to close the branch clean-up issue, how plans are edited, and where criteria live.

handback.summary: Three of the owner's asks have no criterion, and five criteria each hold two cases or two things.

raises.label: No criterion
raises.text: No criterion carries three asks: a re-plan keeps my commits; my work gets the same checks; I edit then say /review. Pin each with a test, or ask the owner.
raises.evidence: Issue: `a re-plan keeps my commits`, `My work goes through the same reviews and checks`; no story names either.

raises.label: Prompt ask reworded
raises.text: Criterion 1.6 turns the owner's prompt ask into a rejection message and bundles two prompts. Make it two criteria: planner prompt says it; worker prompt says it.
raises.evidence: Comment 6132026430: `The planner and worker prompts say: Verified by explains how the test proves the behavior`.

raises.label: Two cases in one
raises.text: Criteria 3.1, 3.2 and 3.3 each hold two cases, no short half or no full half; 3.5 holds names code and past every cap. Split each in two.
raises.evidence: `plan.json` story 3 criteria texts: `no short half or no full half`, `names code and runs past every cap`.

asks.ask: I write tests, as many or as few as I like, or none.
The planner groups tests into criteria, fills gaps with its own tests, and splits work that is too big.
My tests are locked: agents may propose more but never change or drop mine.
my tests cannot be changed by an agent
A plan built on my tests keeps every one unchanged and maps each to a criterion.
A short text for me (capped, plain, no code)
a full text for agents (uncapped, may name code)
anything tied to a test lives in its docstring (first line short, paragraph full) and the record points to the test
raises, stories, Context and questions live in the record as pairs.
Cards show short texts and fold full ones.
The plan reviewer checks each short text matches its full text
each docstring matches what its test does
Every role working on a split story gets the parent's original issue and my comments
A worker on a split story reads the parent's original issue and my comments.
I can add, change or delete tests, plan and code on Dokima's branches, then say /review.
Anything I write counts as my words
a re-plan keeps my commits
My work goes through the same reviews and checks as agent work.
those json models should print out user facing and agent facing information
enforce this as a schema in test files
rigor line let's name it verified by line:
test docstrings user facing and agent facing
Agent holds the full detail, uncapped and folded on cards.
User, Verified by and Edge are short and capped
Each test file opens with the same pair: one user line, then agent detail.
checked by code on new and changed tests only
user facing for tests of course the methodology of testing so you know the rigor of test right of the bat.
please don't use categories finetuned for our repo only that will not fly. think longterm.
verified by and agent should know to explain how test is done so we know instantly the rigor of the test and have comparable expectations
